viewer_sees: MACRO OBJECT — a Han arsenal rack packed with crossbows, ji halberds and iron swords, more weapons than hands to hold them
a Han rider in full lamellar armour on a small shaggy steppe horse whose head hangs low under the weight
CROWD AS TEXTURE — Xiongnu horsemen pouring across the open steppe as one dark moving grain; then one rider close at full gallop, turned in the saddle to loose an arrow backward, no stirrups
Emperor Wu on the palace terrace watching his cavalry drill below on small stocky horses, his face hard
a lone dust-caked traveller walking out of the western desert toward a Han beacon tower, the sentries on its top turning to look

ANIMATED MAP — a silk map unrolled right to left across a lacquered table, the way a Chinese scroll is read: the walls of Chang'an painted at the right end, a thin caravan trail winding west through ink-wash desert and mountain ridges, a green valley ringed by snow peaks at the far left; no writing and no arrows

one magnificent tall red-bay horse on a high mountain pasture from a low angle, a reddish sheen of sweat on the neck and shoulder; long streamers of cloud torn off the ridge above it, only ambiguously like manes
the envoy leading a caravan out of the palace gate toward the west, a golden horse riding on a litter and chests of gold on the carts
the nobles of Dayuan in their hall, one raising his palm to refuse, the golden horse standing untouched on the carpet
Sima Qian at a low table by lamplight, brushing columns onto bamboo slips
an envoy caravan strung out across a salt flat in heat haze, every second camel carrying an empty saddle, fresh stone cairns along the track toward the right edge
a Dayuan noble on the city wall looking east over endless desert and mountains, at ease
the envoy bringing a hammer down on the golden horse, its head breaking from the neck, gold splinters in the air
SILHOUETTE — a small caravan in a mountain pass at dusk, arrows coming down on it from the ridge, the envoy's staff falling
Li Guangli kneeling before the emperor to take the half of a bronze tiger tally, the throne hall quiet
the city of Ershi seen from the valley rim, horse pens packed with tall red horses around its walls
an oasis town with its gate barred and archers on the wall, hungry Han soldiers standing outside it in the dust
a thin column of starving soldiers dragging into a green valley; then the same men broken under arrows at the foot of a border town
LEDGER — a frontier parade ground marked out for rows of ten, only one or two men standing in each row, Li Guangli in front of them
the Jade Gate shut, the emperor's officers on its wall with drawn swords, the ragged army stopped on the desert side
ministers kneeling with foreheads to the floor, the emperor standing over them, turned away
foreign envoys on the palace steps in daylight, each in the dress of his own country, glancing at one another with thin smiles
two ministers in chains led down the palace terrace between guards, while at the foot of the steps new recruits are already forming ranks

CROWD AS TEXTURE — the second army from above as a river of helmets and banners flowing west; then the widest frame of the episode: the whole baggage column of ox carts, horse herds, donkey strings and camel lines as bands of colour running to the horizon under its own dust
a Han village stripped for the war — officials leading away oxen and carts, families watching from their doors
two old horse judges in the army camp, one lifting a horse's hoof, the other running a hand down its leg
the Han army's camps ringing the walls of the Dayuan capital from above, the river running along outside the walls, no well anywhere in the city
from a rise above the city: the wall, the old riverbed along it drying to cracked mud, an earth-and-brushwood dam across it, diggers with baskets, and the river swinging away into a new cut
a breach torn in the outer wall, dust pouring out, Han soldiers climbing the rubble; forty notches cut into a camp post
the nobles in their council hall all turning to look at their king on his throne
seen from the Han siege line: a single noble carrying a closed wooden chest across the open ground from the city gate, Han spear points lowered near the camera
from inside the gateway: tall red horses led out through the open gate toward the Han camp by Dayuan grooms
high over the horse pens inside the walls: a noble with a drawn blade among the tethered horses; far on the horizon the dust of an army coming
Li Guangli in his tent lowering his head once, accepting
the two horse judges picking out the finest red horses from the herd; then the army and three thousand ordinary horses turning east for home
LEDGER — the Jade Gate from above with a thin column coming in through it, the wide road outside empty where sixty thousand had marched out; then the horses coming through behind them
close on Sima Qian's hand and brush pressing one hard stroke onto a bamboo slip, the lamp low
an officer's tent stacked with grain sacks while thin soldiers sit outside with empty bowls
EMPTY AFTERMATH — the throne of Dayuan empty, a cup overturned beside it, a torn Han-silk cushion on the step
a young Dayuan prince arriving at the Han court, two tall red horses led in after him
MACRO OBJECT — the golden horse alone on dark cloth, raking light separating it from the black, in profile, composed like the two living horses of the next shot
two living red horses side by side in a Han stable, in the same profile and at the same height in frame as the golden horse before them, breath in the cold air
the palace roofs rising out of purple-flowering alfalfa that runs to the horizon; then the heavenly horses grazing in it
one heavenly horse alone on a frontier ridge at sunset, a beacon tower far along the wall
END CARD — a heavenly horse and a Han soldier at the Jade Gate at sunset, open sky above for the title
